te: How to study the expropriation bills for the Yellow and Pink Line electric trains
se: The committee set out how to study 3 bills under rule 119 of the Rules of Procedure of the Senate B.E. 2019: the bill on expropriating property to build the electric train of the Nakkharaphiphat (Yellow) Line, the expropriation bill for the Pink Line, Khae Rai–Min Buri, and the bill on placing charges on property for mass transit. The bills have already passed the House of Representatives. The committee also considered requesting supporting documents from agencies.
it: How to study 3 bills under rule 119 (expropriation and charges on property, Yellow and Pink Line electric trains)

te: Train hits a bus at the Asok–Din Daeng level crossing
se: The committee invited the Ministry of Transport, the Department of Rail Transport, the Department of Land Transport, the State Railway of Thailand, the Bangkok Mass Transit Authority, the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration, the Metropolitan Police Bureau and other agencies to explain the case of a freight train hitting a bus and several cars at the level crossing on Asok–Din Daeng Road on 16 May 2026. 8 people died and 30 were injured. The Ministry of Transport set up a fact-finding committee to find the cause, which is under investigation, and plans to reduce freight trains entering inner Bangkok by transferring goods at outer stations and running freight trains mainly at night. The committee considered the safety of level crossings in the city, where vehicles are often stuck on the tracks, and care for those affected.
it: Freight train hitting a bus at the Asok–Din Daeng level crossing (16 May 2026)

te: Topics for talks with the Minister of Transport, and three new subcommittees
se: The committee set 4 main topics for talks with the Minister of Transport and senior officials of the ministry, such as raising safety standards in construction and transport systems and ways to ease the effects of volatile oil prices, and considered setting up 3 new subcommittees.
it: Topics for talks with the Minister of Transport and senior officials (4 topics)
Setting up 3 subcommittees

te: A van operator's complaint at Suvarnabhumi, and the report on the high-speed railway linking three airports
se: The committee considered a complaint by a non-scheduled passenger van operator, who claims unfair treatment because its lease of a service area at Suvarnabhumi Airport was not renewed. Both the complainant and Airports of Thailand (AOT), the state enterprise that runs the airport, were invited to give information. AOT explained its reasons under the terms of the contract, such as vehicle inspections. The committee listened in order to find a fair solution. It also considered the report on the high-speed railway linking three airports as a public–private partnership (PPP).
it: Complaint by a non-scheduled passenger van operator about a lease of space at Suvarnabhumi Airport (a claim)
Report on the high-speed railway linking three airports (PPP)

te: Choosing speakers for the debate on the Cabinet's policy statement
se: The committee considered its share and its representatives for the joint sitting of Parliament to hear the Cabinet's policy statement under section 162 of the Constitution. Speakers are of 2 kinds: those speaking under their own privilege and those representing the committee. Consideration of the high-speed railway reports was moved to the next meeting.
it: The committee's share and representatives in the debate on the Cabinet's policy statement (section 162)

te: Setting up new subcommittees, and a study visit to Satun and Krabi
se: The committee discussed how to set up subcommittees to consider matters within the powers and duties of the Committee on Transportation, giving members the chance to propose topics to study, and considered the schedule for a study visit to Satun and Krabi.
it: How to set up subcommittees
Schedule for a study visit to Satun and Krabi

te: Review of the Land Bridge study, and the Thai–Chinese high-speed railway report
se: The committee considered a report that checks the assumptions of the project for an economic land bridge between the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman Sea (Land Bridge) on technical, economic, logistics and legal grounds, in 6 areas such as time and cost savings, the feasibility of transferring containers, the expected volume of cargo, and competition, so that policy decisions are careful and consider the country's long-term interest. The committee also considered the study report on the Thai–Chinese high-speed railway and agreed to submit it to the Senate.
it: Report checking the assumptions of the Land Bridge project (6 areas)
Study report on the Thai–Chinese high-speed railway

te: High-speed railway study visit and progress of the drone subcommittee
se: The committee heard the chair's report on the study visit to the high-speed railway project and the progress of the subcommittee studying the high-speed railway linking three airports and phase 1 of the Thai–Chinese high-speed railway, and the progress of the subcommittee studying unmanned aircraft (drones) and the other subcommittees.
it: Results of the study visit to the high-speed railway project
Progress of the subcommittees (high-speed railway, drones and others)

te: Air fares, passenger rights and crowding at airports
se: The committee considered air transport, including fares, passenger rights and the allocation of take-off and landing slots, with Airports of Thailand (AOT) and the airline association invited. AOT explained that it uses technology to reduce crowding, such as self check-in and bag drop, automatic passport control and Airport Collaborative Decision Making (Airport CDM) at Suvarnabhumi and Don Mueang since March 2024, which raised on-time performance at Suvarnabhumi from 73 to 84 per cent, with plans to extend it to Phuket and Chiang Mai, as well as plans to expand airport capacity.
it: Fares, passenger rights and slot allocation (AOT and the airline association)

te: Report on preventing and reducing accidents on land, water and in the air
se: The committee heard the findings of the subcommittee studying ways to prevent and reduce transport accidents on land, on water and in the air. The main causes of road accidents are speeding, drinking alcohol and other intoxicants, cutting in too closely, and ignoring traffic signs, and the subcommittee made recommendations to prevent and reduce losses. The committee also heard progress on the study of the high-speed railway projects.
it: Findings on ways to prevent and reduce transport accidents
Progress of the study of the high-speed railway projects

te: Crane parts from high-speed railway construction fall on a train at Sikhio, and the Rama 2 Road incident
se: The committee invited the agencies concerned to explain the incident of 14 January 2026, when the front support of a launching girder crane of the Thai–Chinese high-speed railway project, weighing about 40–50 tonnes, fell onto a passenger train in Sikhio District, Nakhon Ratchasima, while the contractor was moving the equipment to its next position. 30 people died and 69 were injured. The agencies reported initial compensation for the families of those who died, about 1,773,000 baht per person in total, from the contractor, the project's insurer and the State Railway of Thailand. The committee also heard the Department of Highways on the collapse of the Bang Khun Thian–Ban Phaeo elevated road (Motorway 82) in Mueang Samut Sakhon District on 15 January 2026, in which 2 workers died and 2 were injured. Experts' initial checks found a progressive collapse of the structure. The committee stressed raising safety standards in infrastructure construction.
it: Crane parts from high-speed railway construction falling onto a passenger train, Sikhio District, Nakhon Ratchasima (14 January 2026)
Collapse of the Bang Khun Thian–Ban Phaeo elevated road (M82), Mueang Samut Sakhon District (15 January 2026)

te: Progress on the Thai–Chinese high-speed railway and the subcommittees' work
se: The committee heard progress reports from its subcommittees. The subcommittee studying the high-speed railway linking three airports and phase 1 of the Thai–Chinese high-speed railway (Bangkok–Nakhon Ratchasima) reported that the State Railway of Thailand still faces several obstacles, such as permission to use government land, land expropriation, design changes and delays in some contracts. Contracts 3-1 and 3-2 are awaiting permission to use forest land in Saraburi, and expropriation under contract 3-1 has only 3 plots left, with the land expected to be handed over by February 2026. The committee also heard progress from the subcommittees on water transport and on accident prevention.
it: Progress of phase 1 of the Thai–Chinese high-speed railway and the high-speed railway linking three airports
Progress of the other subcommittees

te: Meeting 3/2569 · Subcommittee to Study Ways to Prevent and Reduce Transport Accidents
Meeting 2/2569 · Subcommittee to Study Ways to Prevent and Reduce Transport Accidents
Meeting 1/2569 · Subcommittee to Study Ways to Prevent and Reduce Transport Accidents
Transport and logistics links to deep-sea ports on the Andaman coast
se: Meeting on Thursday 19 November 2026 at 09.30 hrs, Committee Meeting Room CA 427, floor 4, Parliament House. The agenda is to study the policies, plans and ways to develop transport and logistics networks that link deep-sea ports on the Andaman Sea coast with economic areas and the national transport network. Representatives of the Department of Rail Transport, the State Railway of Thailand, the Department of Highways and the Department of Rural Roads are invited to give information and views, as set out in the meeting notice. A summary will be added after the Senate publishes the meeting summary.
it: Policies, plans and ways to develop transport and logistics networks linking deep-sea ports on the Andaman Sea coast with economic areas and the national transport network
